samples.summary: The only doc hunk in this change states the slides surface "has no persona yet", but the same change adds the `slide-author` persona (personas.json) and its charter (`scripts/agent/charters-ui/slide-author.md`). The persona table above it (line 98–103, "Two personas, each with two briefs") is also left stale — it omits `slide-author` / `arrange-and-order` / `content-and-undo`. The canonical usage doc therefore actively contradicts the shipped configuration, and `scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs:47` ("no persona explores `s`") proves a persona per surface is required, so the doc's "adding one is the next step" is false on this very branch. Docs discipline: update the existing doc to match, not to describe a prior intermediate state.

samples.summary: The canonical subsystem doc for the UI hunter (Phase 31, `docs/design/harness-engineering.md`) still describes the bridge as a closed registry of `doc.*` / `sheet.*` readers over `MemStore`/`MemDocStore` with the `DocsFormattingToolbar` mounted. This change adds a third surface with six new readers, a lazily-loaded engine, a hand-authored seed and a new persona — an extension of the hunter's architecture — and does not record any of it there. Per CONTRIBUTING the existing canonical doc should be updated rather than the change being documented only in the usage doc (which itself now contradicts it).
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:2883-2886 enumerates `doc.text`, `doc.runs`, `doc.fontSizes`, `sheet.cellValue`, `sheet.cellCenter`, `doc.canUndo`, `sheet.canUndo` "over `MemStore`/`MemDocStore`, with the real `DocsFormattingToolbar` mounted" — no mention of the slides surface, its readers, or the on-demand engine load.

samples.summary: `covers()` re-implements a point-in-frame test that already ships as an exported helper: `containsPoint(frame, px, py)` from `@wafflebase/slides` (packages/slides/src/model/frame.ts:10, re-exported at packages/slides/src/index.ts:144), which additionally accounts for rotation. The seed module's stated reason for having no imports is unit-test weight, which is a real constraint, but the divergence is worth noting: the seed's axis-aligned, edge-inclusive rect check is a different predicate from the canvas's real hit test (`hitTestSlide`/`hitTestElement`, which honours ellipse geometry — and `badge` is an ellipse), so the invariant the test pins is only an approximation of the rule it claims to enforce.
samples.evidence: slides-seed.ts:41 `export function covers(frame, point)` duplicates packages/slides/src/model/frame.ts:10 `export function containsPoint(frame: Frame, px, py)`.

samples.summary: The change's own commentary makes "stop restating the surface vocabulary" its theme (hunt-ui-probe.mjs "FIFTH copy", hunt-ui-runner.mjs "SIXTH copy"), yet it adds two more restatements on the frontend side: `HuntSurface = "sheet" | "doc" | "slides"` in bridge.ts and the new `SURFACES` array in page.tsx. The arch lint boundary plausibly forbids importing `scripts/agent/hunt-ui-surfaces.mjs` from frontend source, but nothing here derives one list from the other or asserts they agree, so the frontend copies can drift from `UI_SURFACES` exactly the way the script copies did.
samples.evidence: page.tsx:70 `const SURFACES: readonly HuntSurface[] = ["sheet", "doc", "slides"];` alongside bridge.ts:35 `export type HuntSurface = "sheet" | "doc" | "slides";` versus scripts/agent/hunt-ui-surfaces.mjs:33.

samples.summary: The new slides reader expectations hardcode the seed's values (`"card,badge,title,body"`, `title.x === 160`, `w === 1600`, text `"Quarterly review"`, `slideCount === 2`) rather than deriving them from `slides-seed.ts` / `page.tsx`, so the seed geometry now lives in three places (SEED_FRAMES, the oracle expectations, and the charter markdown's "measured" facts). A .mjs script cannot import the .ts seed without a build step, so this may be unavoidable, but a seed edit will now require three coordinated updates and only one of them is mechanically checked.

verdict.reason: The claim is accurate as described. docs/design/hunter-usage.md:98-103 still says "Two personas, each with two briefs" and lists only `doc-writer` and `sheet-author`; :105-109 explicitly states the `slides` surface "has no persona yet, so nothing hunts it" and "Adding one is the next step". Meanwhile scripts/agent/charters-ui/personas.json:49-94 ships a `slide-author` persona with `"surface": "slides"` and two briefs (`arrange-and-order` :61, `content-and-undo` :65), with a matching charter at scripts/agent/charters-ui/slide-author.md. scripts/agent/hunt-ui.test.mjs:44-47 enforces that every surface in UI_SURFACES has a persona ("no persona explores `${s}`"), so the doc's "next step" wording is not merely stale but contradicted by a shipped invariant. Under the design-fit lens this is a design-doc discipline / spec-conformance violation (canonical doc must be updated to match the change, not left describing a prior intermediate state) and is major, not taste. No guard or caller makes the prose unreachable.
